title: Apple’s Cheap MacBook Neo Made a Splash — Now Everyone Wants to Copy It!
summary:
Remember when Apple dropped the MacBook Neo for just $599? It was like throwing a giant boulder into a pond — huge ripples everywhere! Now, other companies are trying to make their own splash. Dell just announced a new XPS 13 that looks a lot like the Neo. It’s made of shiny aluminum, super thin, and has a bright, sharp screen. It even starts at $699 (or $599 for students) with 8 GB of memory, just like the Neo. But here’s the cool part: you can upgrade the Dell to have more memory and storage later, which the Neo won’t let you do.

Then there’s Microsoft. They’re planning a new Surface Laptop with only 8 GB of memory, but it might cost $1,200! That’s double the price of the Neo, and it doesn’t even have a fancy new design. It feels like Microsoft saw Apple’s success and thought, “Hey, let’s just use less memory and call it a day!” But that misses the point. The Neo works because it’s cheap and feels premium. Dell gets it. Microsoft? Not so much. The laptop world is getting wild, and soon we might even see $300 Windows laptops. Buckle up!
why_it_matters: Knowing what makes a laptop a good deal will help you choose a better one when it's time for your own computer, maybe even saving your family money.
